findings.reason: Approved ML-74 requires 0 ≤ ε < (1−γ)⁻¹, while the current definition and both PAC-bound statements supply finite bounds only for ε > 0. Their proofs use inverse-ε thresholds and set ε₁ proportional to ε, so they do not establish a finite zero-tolerance bound; the hypotheses also impose no quantitative action-gap lower bound. Strehl’s formal PAC definitions require ε > 0, although Theorems 11 and 16 display a zero endpoint [in the JMLR paper, §1.5 and Theorems 11, 16](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume10/strehl09a/strehl09a.pdf). Owner reconciliation is required for this definition, both bound theorems, ex-pac-mdp-discount-factor-dependence, and ex-pac-mdp-delayed-q-zero-slack.
